title: What If We Learned to See with More Than One Perspective?
excerpt:
Bartlett, Marshall, and Marshall’s article on Two-Eyed Seeing made me reflect on a simple but demanding idea: meaningful understanding may require more than one way of seeing.

Mi'kmaw Elder Albert Marshall introduced Two-Eyed Seeing, or Etuaptmumk. It encourages us to learn from the strengths of Indigenous knowledge with one eye and from the strengths of Western knowledge with the other, and to use both together for everyone's benefit. Importantly, the approach recognizes each knowledge system as distinct rather than requiring one to be absorbed into the other.

title: Renewable Energy Is Growing. But Who Owns the Transition?
excerpt: The transition to renewable energy is an unquestionable step toward a more sustainable future. Solar, wind, hydro, and other renewable technologies can reduce dependence on fossil fuels and help mitigate climate change. Yet the article by Christina Hoicka, Katarina Savic, and Alicia Campney, “Reconciliation through renewable energy? A survey of Indigenous communities, involvement, and peoples in Canada,” urges us to look beyond the technology itself.
